belief: No one could be attracted to me.
origins: Rejection, comparisons, or scarring can make us believe romance is out of reach. We may avoid dating, friendships, or intimacy to avoid being hurt.
teaches: “You are altogether beautiful, my darling; in you there is no flaw” (Song of Solomon 4:7) captures how love sees. “Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting.” “Man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.” Attraction is rarely about a single measure. Kindness, humor, faithfulness, and shared faith draw people. Many people are loved deeply by someone who sees them fully. God can work in His time, and meanwhile you are loved.
self_statements: No one will ever want me.
I am not the type anyone falls for.
People like me do not get loved.
errors: Believing people are either attractive or not.
Predicting that no one will want me.
Feeling unattractive and concluding that I am.
questions: What draws me to others besides looks?
Who in my life has been loved deeply who did not fit a standard?
What qualities do I bring to a relationship?
What fears keep me from reaching out?
What does Scripture say about how love sees?
What first step would feel safe?
truth: Attraction is more than appearance, and love sees the whole person. I have qualities worth loving, and I can take safe steps toward friendship and connection, trusting God with the rest.
hw_truths: I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
I can take a safe step.
log: Each week, note one friendly step you took.
prayer: Lord, I fear no one will want me. Remind me that love sees the heart, and lead me gently toward connection in Your time. Amen.
